clue.text: Player added a bit of cream to hair

indicators.note: added ... to says the earlier pieces are joined on before the next one
a bit of the word cream is just its opening letter

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Someone working a dab of cream into their hair while getting ready.
explanation.definitionFit: A player is a performer on stage, and a woman who acts is one such performer.

clue.text: Question many on trial

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, i.e. many
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: A query about how many people are being tried in court.
explanation.definitionFit: To question a claim is to dispute or challenge it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Soldier's pretence of dissent

parts.note: RE (Royal Engineers) stands for soldiers; the 's is read as 'is' joining on
an act is a pretence, as in putting on an act

explanation.surface: A soldier only pretending to object.
explanation.definitionFit: To react against something is to respond in opposition, so dissent is a fair verb synonym.

clue.text: Study group in airmen's mess

indicators.note: a mess is a jumble, so these letters are thrown into a new order; also a forces dining room in the surface

explanation.surface: A study group meeting in the RAF mess hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' reads as the airmen's canteen, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminar is a class where a small group of students discuss a subject.

clue.text: Girl eats dace cooked in college

indicators.note: eats has one piece taking the other into its middle

parts.note: Amy is a girl's name

indicators.note: cooked means the fish's letters are prepared into a new order

explanation.surface: A girl at college eating fish cooked in the canteen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' looks like part of the dinner scene but signals the rearrangement of the fish's name.
explanation.definitionFit: An academy is a school or college of higher learning.

clue.text: Creditor possesses coins

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for creditor
owns means possesses

explanation.surface: A moneylender who holds a stock of coins.
explanation.definitionFit: A crown is an old British coin worth five shillings.

clue.text: Trim blue carpet

parts.note: to dress is to trim, as in dressing a hedge or timber
down means blue, i.e. sad

explanation.surface: Trimming a blue rug to fit the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carpet' is the verb: to carpet someone is to reprimand them.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is to scold them, an idiom matching the reprimanding sense.

clue.text: Sailor gives lashings in support of officer

indicators.note: in a down entry a piece in support of another sits below it

parts.note: a mate is a ship's officer
lashings means a lot, plenty

explanation.surface: A sailor flogged at the behest of an officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lashings' suggests floggings at sea; here it is the informal sense of plenty.
explanation.definitionFit: Matelot is British slang for a seaman, from the French word.

clue.text: Arrangement for lecture about royal box

indicators.note: about has the speech wrapping round the other pieces

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech or lecture
a chest is a box

explanation.surface: Planning a talk about the royal box at the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Orchestration is the arranging of music for an orchestra, hence an arrangement.

clue.text: South American seen in Dublin Castle

indicators.note: seen in says the letters are on view inside the words Dublin Castle

explanation.surface: A South American tourist spotted at Dublin Castle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Incas were the native people of Peru who built an Andean empire.

clue.text: "I'm to enter a new arrangement", articulated performer

indicators.note: a new arrangement of these quoted words reorders their letters

explanation.surface: A performer quoted as agreeing to join a fresh deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A puppet worked by strings has jointed limbs, so it is a performer that is literally articulated.

clue.text: Current fashion for scientist

parts.note: new means current, up to date
the ton is old-fashioned for high fashion

explanation.surface: The latest trend among scientists.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Newton was the English physicist who described gravity.

clue.text: Plant encircles lake? No kidding!

indicators.note: encircles has the plant name go round the other letter

parts.note: honesty is a garden plant with papery seed pods
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Disbelief that a plant could grow right round a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation meaning 'truly, I mean it', the same as no kidding.

clue.text: Latest news of holy woman's put down

parts.note: ST is short for saint, a holy woman; the 's reads as 'is'
to oppress is to put down or subjugate

explanation.surface: A newspaper flash about a nun being suppressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Stop press is late news added to a paper after printing has begun.

clue.text: Cope with freak distribution? That gives nothing away!

indicators.note: distribution spreads these letters out into a new order

explanation.surface: Handling a bizarre deal of the cards without betraying anything.
explanation.definitionFit: An expressionless face hides one's thoughts, as a card player must.

clue.text: Prize for lad keeping books

indicators.note: keeping has the young man hold the other letters within

parts.note: a lad is a boy
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A trophy for a schoolboy who looks after the books.
explanation.definitionFit: Booty is plunder taken in war, a prize seized from the enemy.

clue.text: Gives a drenching to drunkards

definitions.meaning: heavy drinkers are informally called this

explanation.surface: Soaking the town drunks with water.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for wetting through and a slang noun for boozers.

clue.text: Prevent honoured officer adopting the Roman way to tango

indicators.note: adopting has the award letters take the others into their middle

parts.note: an OBE is an Officer of the Order of the British Empire, an honour
via is Latin for way, as in Via Appia
T is tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A decorated officer heading off a dance by learning it the Roman way.
explanation.definitionFit: To obviate is to remove a need or prevent a difficulty in advance.

clue.text: Host attending the Queen

parts.note: present means attending, being there
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A hostess accompanying the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The host of a TV show introduces it, the job of a broadcast frontman.

clue.text: Birds for every one in Wales

parts.note: swans are birds
EA is short for each, meaning for every one

explanation.surface: Birds allotted one apiece somewhere in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Swansea is a city on the south coast of Wales, so it lies in that country.

clue.text: Range of vessels in river

indicators.note: in puts the cooking vessels inside the river name

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, England
pans are cooking vessels

explanation.surface: A set of boats spread across a river.
explanation.definitionFit: An expanse is a wide stretch or extent, just as a range is.

clue.text: Optical device advanced artist

parts.note: came means advanced, moved forward
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter at the cutting edge of optical gadgets.
explanation.definitionFit: A camera uses a lens to form images, a classic optical instrument.

clue.text: Finished with model? That's a bit dim!

parts.note: over means finished
a cast is a model made from a mould

explanation.surface: Mocking a model as not very bright after the shoot ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A sky full of cloud is gloomy, so the light is somewhat dim.

clue.text: Rub Pat the wrong way? That's sudden!

indicators.note: rubbing the wrong way disorders these letters

explanation.surface: Annoying someone called Pat with a curt manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Abrupt means sudden and unexpected, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Registers car

definitions.meaning: lists or records, as in electoral lists

explanation.surface: Signing up a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Official lists are rolls, and a Rolls is the short name for a Rolls-Royce motor.

clue.text: Scoundrels about to claim Oxford University is like death

indicators.note: about has the rogues go round the rest

parts.note: cads are scoundrels
to aver is to claim

explanation.surface: Rogues insisting that Oxford is deathly.
explanation.definitionFit: Cadaverous means corpse-like, pale and gaunt, so resembling a dead body.

clue.text: Dragging a piece of timber around Norwegian capital

indicators.note: around has the timber wrap round the other letter

parts.note: a log is a piece of timber

indicators.note: the capital of the word Norwegian is its initial letter

explanation.surface: Hauling a log around Oslo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Norwegian capital' wants to be Oslo; it is only the first letter of Norwegian.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dragging goes on tediously and lasts too much time.

clue.text: A number embrace goddess? That's capital!

indicators.note: embrace has the number go round the goddess

parts.note: ten is a number
Hera was the Greek queen of the gods

explanation.surface: A crowd hugging a goddess, greeted with a cry of approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital!' looks like an exclamation of delight; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Teheran, also spelt Tehran, is the chief city and seat of government of Iran.

clue.text: Woman in torment shows spirit

indicators.note: in puts the female pronoun inside the word for torment

parts.note: a bane is a torment or curse
she refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A woman in agony revealing her spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: In Irish folklore a banshee is a female spirit who wails to foretell a death.
